task: Close the remaining Control Plane Unit 3 execution gap by binding every release unit to a canonical child Development Transaction and by adding a thin GitHub-bound execution adapter that consumes the Unit 2 manifest, existing materializer, existing Truth/Lifecycle receipts and exact merge identity without closing the parent transaction early or creating parallel release/proof authority.

operationalIntelligence.problemStatement: Merged Unit 3 provides a fail-closed release-unit state machine and validates materialization, PR, Truth/Lifecycle and merge receipts, but it still consumes operator-supplied execution events rather than producing them. More critically, intermediate unit verification accepts any closed Lifecycle receipt at the PR head without binding that receipt to a distinct child Development Transaction, so a unit can only be represented by either falsely closing the parent plan or by consuming an unbound synthetic child lifecycle. The required end-to-end multi-unit Development Transaction is therefore not yet machine-executable without manual branch/plan/receipt reconstruction.
observableOutcomes: Each release-unit manifest carries a canonical child Development Transaction projection produced upstream by Plan Before Code before sealing, so downstream execution does not rediscover scope, risk, gates, proof ownership, domain/authority, Known Failure or Negative Knowledge obligations.

A release-unit PR can run the existing Knowledge, Plan Before Code, Edit-Time, Incremental Replay, Release Risk, Quality, TypeScript, Build, external-proof applicability, Completion Truth and Lifecycle machinery against an ephemeral manifest-bound child plan while the parent Development Transaction remains open.
Unit verification rejects Truth or Lifecycle evidence whose task/parent/unit/manifest identity does not match the exact child transaction and exact PR head.

A thin GitHub-bound adapter uses the existing atomic release-unit materializer, pushes the exact materialized commit, creates an exact-base PR, consumes exact-head canonical proof artifacts, records the merge receipt, reconciles the resulting main and advances only the next authorized unit.
Execution state is persisted with compare-and-swap identity so interruption/resume never requires an operator to reconstruct branch, child plan, PR, proof or predecessor state by hand.
After U1/U2 child lifecycle closure the parent stays in EXECUTE; only all unit CLOSED states permit the existing parent Completion Truth/Lifecycle closure.
unresolvedRisks: A child plan must be usable by existing guards without becoming a second repository-wide active-plan authority or being accidentally merged over the parent plan.

PR metadata is mutable, so any transport for an ephemeral child plan must be cryptographically bound to the exact materialized commit and sealed manifest rather than trusted as free-form operator input.
GitHub merge/squash/rebase can produce a new main SHA distinct from the verified PR head, so the adapter must preserve the existing explicit source-head-to-resulting-main receipt semantics.
A persisted orchestration state ref can race with retries or a second operator; state updates therefore require exact expected-ref compare-and-swap and fail closed on drift.
The GitHub adapter must reuse existing gh/Git credentials and may not become a new token/permission authority or bypass branch/CI policy.

in: Extend Plan Before Code release-unit manifests with a sealed child Development Transaction projection and digest before manifestDigest is finalized.
Allow the existing core development guard scripts to consume an explicit SHOPERATION_ACTIVE_PLAN path while preserving the root active-plan default and canonical semantics.
Add a release-unit CI context resolver that accepts only a manifest-bound, exact-head child plan envelope and exports the alternate active-plan path for existing gates.

Add child-lifecycle mode to the existing closure machinery so an ephemeral release-unit child plan closes into an execution receipt/artifact rather than requiring a repository active-plan commit; parent closure semantics remain unchanged.
Strengthen release-unit verification so Truth/Lifecycle task identity, parent transaction identity, releaseUnitId, manifestDigest and exact source head must match the projected child transaction.

Add a thin GitHub-bound execution adapter over existing materializeReleaseUnit plus git/gh: state-ref CAS, exact unit branch push, PR create/read, exact-head proof receipt import, exact-head merge, resulting-main receipt and successor authorization/reconciliation.

Add adversarial regressions for parent/child lifecycle separation, tampered PR context, stale state ref, wrong proof task, wrong PR head/base/source, GitHub/gh failure, merge drift, duplicate retries, successor obligation drift and interruption/resume.

Route Sentinel integrity probe plan consumption through the same validated alternate child-plan path so Incremental Replay cannot silently inspect the parent plan during a child Development Transaction.

Preserve critical semantic-route assurance for create-only child release units by allowing a manifest-bound child transaction to satisfy the route target requirement through mustCreate when mustEdit is empty; root critical transactions retain the existing mustEdit requirement.
Upgrade the existing Unit 3 orchestration regression fixtures to the mandatory child transaction identity so no legacy unbound verification path remains accepted.

Place the GitHub-bound release execution runtime under the canonical DOMAIN-RELEASE scripts/release-** ownership path; do not add a DOMAIN-QUALITY→DOMAIN-RELEASE exception merely to preserve an incorrectly located helper.

Synchronize the existing Operational Intelligence lifecycle regression with the new child-lifecycle branch so Reference Sync proves both root BLOCK_UNTIL_COMMITTED semantics and child receipt emission semantics.
out: No new Completion Truth, Lifecycle, Release Risk, Atlas, Sentinel, CI/CD, deployment or production release authority.
No weakening of branch protection, exact-head evidence, Security Audit, Template Factory applicability, Release Risk Budget, Known Failure replay or Failure Intake.
No per-file GitHub Contents API materialization; Unit 2 atomic Git tree/commit materialization remains the only code transplant path.
No automatic production deployment, Supabase mutation, product runtime change, auth change, commerce change, Builder/template change or Vercel promotion.
No automatic Knowledge/Negative Knowledge promotion solely because this hardening is implemented.

assuranceCeiling.rationale: This change controls execution provenance across child transactions, PR creation, proof import and merge progression. A false binding could allow a green but unrelated PR or lifecycle receipt to advance a multi-unit parent, so deterministic identity, adversarial state-machine proof, exact-head provenance and fail-closed external command behavior are mandatory.

acceptanceCriteria: Every release unit receives a deterministic child taskId and child-plan digest that is included in the canonical release-unit manifest before manifestDigest/sealing.
Child Plan Before Code consumes upstream manifest-projected scope facts and rejects context/plan/manifest drift; it does not silently reconstruct a wider or different unit.

Existing guards read an explicit alternate child-plan path only when a validated release-unit CI context enables it; ordinary repository transactions continue to use quality/development/active-plan.json unchanged.
Child Completion Truth and Lifecycle closure are exact-head and exact-task bound, and Unit 3 recordReleaseUnitVerification rejects parent-plan or foreign-unit receipts.
Closing U1/U2 child transactions never marks the parent Development Transaction closed or LEARN.

The GitHub adapter can initialize/resume exact persisted execution state, materialize the current authorized unit, push the exact commit, create/read the matching PR, import exact proof, merge only the verified source head and record resulting main SHA.

A stale execution state ref, stale main, mutable/tampered PR context, PR head/base drift, missing gh authentication, non-success proof, missing child closure, or merge result drift blocks without advancing state.
After merge, a successor can advance only from a freshly produced/reconciled manifest and child transaction bound to the new main.

A three-unit integration replay completes U1→U2→U3 with separate child closures while parent closureEligible remains false until U3 closes and parent Completion Truth/Lifecycle remains the sole final closure authority.
Sentinel integrity checks executed inside a child transaction consume the validated child plan path; root/default runs remain bound to quality/development/active-plan.json.
A create-only release unit can form a valid critical child Development Transaction without inventing a fake mustEdit target, while non-child critical plans still require canonical mustEdit coverage.
Legacy release-unit executions without canonical childDevelopmentTransaction identity are rejected by VERIFIED transition rather than grandfathered through a compatibility bypass.

Atlas classifies scripts/release-unit-github-runtime.mjs as DOMAIN-RELEASE/release-infrastructure and authority reconciliation contains no policy exception for the former scripts/lib/shoperation-* location.

The lifecycle regression asserts that root plans still emit BLOCK_UNTIL_COMMITTED/candidate behavior while manifest-bound child plans emit a PASS child lifecycle receipt without mutating the parent/root active plan.
invariants: Unit 2 manifest remains code scope authority; the GitHub adapter cannot add product operations beyond the sealed manifest.
Child transaction metadata is derived by the Plan Before Code producer and cryptographically bound to manifest/commit identity; free-form PR text is never authority.
Child lifecycle closure is not parent lifecycle closure and cannot mutate the canonical parent plan status.
The exact materialized commit equals the PR source HEAD used for proof; any later code commit invalidates verification.
The merge receipt separately binds verified sourceHeadSha and resulting mergedMainSha for merge/squash/rebase semantics.
Persistent execution-state updates require exact expected-ref CAS; concurrent or stale writers fail closed.
The adapter uses existing git/gh authentication and never stores or invents credentials.
Successor risk/gate/proof/authority/generated-artifact/dependency obligations come from a fresh canonical producer result, not adapter-side recomputation.

failureModes: Unit verification consumes the parent active-plan closure receipt or another unit's green Truth because task identity is not checked.
The adapter creates a PR from a branch whose head changed after materialization.
A PR body child-plan envelope is edited without changing code and a workflow consumes the mutated plan as authority.
Two resumed operators write different next states to the execution ref and the later writer silently overwrites the first.
GitHub reports PR merge success but main no longer equals the merge result by the time successor reconciliation begins.
A predecessor merge changes current-main obligations but successor reuses the old child plan/manifest.
gh/git is unavailable or unauthenticated and the adapter manufactures a local receipt instead of stopping.
edgeCases: ALREADY_APPLIED unit materialization where the exact base already contains all unit operations must still bind a deterministic execution/proof identity or fail closed if no distinct PR is meaningful.
Squash/rebase merge returns a main SHA different from source head but still has valid exact source-head provenance.
External Template Factory proof is applicable for one child unit but not another; child gate obligations must follow each canonical manifest.
A unit contains only tests/control-plane files and remains a real child transaction rather than being silently collapsed into parent metadata.
Execution resumes after process interruption with an existing PR or already merged predecessor and must be idempotent only when all exact identities match.

alternatives.summary: Commit each child plan into quality/development/active-plan.json on the release-unit branch and restore the parent around merge.
alternatives.reason: It makes PR HEAD contain control metadata outside the Unit 2 code scope, risks merging a child plan over the parent, and couples child closure to repository-plan commits.

alternatives.summary: Keep parent active-plan unchanged and let the release-unit orchestrator issue its own VERIFIED/CLOSED verdicts.
alternatives.reason: It creates the parallel Truth/Lifecycle authority explicitly forbidden by the ecosystem design.

alternatives.summary: Have Plan Before Code project a child transaction into the canonical manifest, transport it as exact-head-bound CI context, and run existing guards/Truth/Lifecycle against that alternate plan while persisting orchestration receipts separately.
alternatives.reason: It preserves the parent plan, keeps Unit 2 as scope authority, reuses existing proof engines, and enables exact machine execution without product-scope widening.

specialistReviews.finding: The missing capability is producer/consumer integration and child transaction identity, not a new release manager.
specialistReviews.resolution: Extend the existing release-unit manifest/runtime and development-plan path plumbing; keep Release Transaction and Completion Truth authorities unchanged.

specialistReviews.finding: Current recordReleaseUnitVerification accepts a closed lifecycle at the correct head without checking that Truth/Lifecycle belong to the release unit; tests can therefore inject a synthetic closed plan and accidentally model parent closure.
specialistReviews.resolution: Introduce deterministic child task identity and require truth.taskId plus lifecycle child binding to match releaseUnit execution identity before VERIFIED.

specialistReviews.finding: Current orchestrator consumes PR/merge receipts but no repository producer creates those receipts, leaving manual branch/PR/merge reconstruction.
specialistReviews.resolution: Add a thin exact-identity git/gh adapter over the existing materializer and persist execution state with CAS; do not implement another materializer or release-risk evaluator.

specialistReviews.finding: Mutable PR metadata cannot itself be execution authority and GitHub credentials must not become repository data.
specialistReviews.resolution: Bind child-plan context digest into the materialized commit and sealed manifest; validate PR head/context equality and use only existing gh/git credential channels.

challenge.scenario: U1 Truth is VERIFIED at the right SHA but taskId is the parent transaction.
challenge.finding: Current Unit 3 could accept it and conflate child completion with parent completion.
challenge.resolution: Unit verification requires exact child taskId, parentTransactionId, releaseUnitId and manifestDigest binding.

challenge.scenario: U1 lifecycle plan is closed/LEARN but belongs to U2.
challenge.finding: Head equality alone is not sufficient provenance.
challenge.resolution: Child lifecycle receipt must expose and match child task/release-unit identity plus exact verifiedImplementationHead.

challenge.scenario: Child plan is transported in PR metadata and edited after materialization.
challenge.finding: Mutable metadata could silently alter gates/scope without changing PR HEAD.
challenge.resolution: Canonical child-plan/context digest is produced before materialization, carried in manifest and commit trailer, and CI rejects any envelope whose digest differs.

challenge.scenario: Adapter is asked to add an extra code file while opening the PR.
challenge.finding: That would widen Unit 2 manifest authority.
challenge.resolution: PR branch is pushed directly from the atomic materialized commit; adapter accepts no arbitrary file mutation input.

challenge.scenario: PR branch receives another commit after materialization.
challenge.finding: A green PR could no longer prove the authorized materialized transaction.
challenge.resolution: All PR create/read/proof/merge transitions require headSha equal materializedHeadSha; mismatch is STALE/BLOCK.

challenge.scenario: CI is green but child Truth artifact is absent or task-mismatched.
challenge.finding: Workflow success is weaker than Completion Truth.
challenge.resolution: Adapter imports and validates existing Truth + child lifecycle artifacts; status checks alone never set VERIFIED.

challenge.scenario: Two processes resume the same parent state and both attempt U2.
challenge.finding: Parallel writers can fork activeUnit/state.
challenge.resolution: Persistent execution state has an exact expected state-ref commit lease and compare-and-swap update.

challenge.scenario: gh is missing, unauthenticated, or returns malformed JSON.
challenge.finding: Fabricating a receipt would break provenance.
challenge.resolution: External command adapter treats missing/nonzero/malformed responses as failure and never advances persisted state.

challenge.scenario: PR merge API returns success using squash and source head differs from resulting main.
challenge.finding: Equality of source and main would reject valid strategy or lose successor base.
challenge.resolution: Keep existing explicit merge receipt with sourceHeadSha and mergedMainSha; successor binds only to mergedMainSha.

challenge.scenario: Main advances after merge result before successor authorization.
challenge.finding: Successor could absorb unrelated drift.
challenge.resolution: Fresh main must equal predecessor mergedMainSha at reconciliation; otherwise STALE/fail closed.

challenge.scenario: U1 child plan closes successfully.
challenge.finding: Parent must not become DONE/LEARN.
challenge.resolution: Child closure is stored only as unit verification receipt; synchronizeReleaseParentExecution keeps parent lifecyclePhase EXECUTE while any unit is not CLOSED.

challenge.scenario: Fresh U2 manifest changes gates/proof/dependencies/generated identity.
challenge.finding: Old child plan is stale even if branch path names are unchanged.
challenge.resolution: Successor child transaction must be projected from the fresh canonical manifest after merge, and old digest cannot authorize the new unit.

challenge.scenario: Adapter resumes and finds the exact PR already open.
challenge.finding: Duplicate PR creation is unnecessary but should not force failure.
challenge.resolution: Resume is idempotent only when PR number/head/base/context/source identity all match; otherwise fail closed.

challenge.scenario: Adapter resumes after the exact PR is already merged.
challenge.finding: Re-merging is invalid but state may lag.
challenge.resolution: It may reconcile only from an authoritative matching merged PR receipt/resulting main; mismatched merge provenance blocks.

challenge.scenario: Final U3 is closed but parent Truth is not VERIFIED.
challenge.finding: Unit chain completion is not parent completion.
challenge.resolution: Parent becomes closureEligible only; existing parent Truth/Lifecycle remains required for closureComplete.

challenge.scenario: A release unit is ALREADY_APPLIED on current main.
challenge.finding: There may be no meaningful code PR head distinct from main.
challenge.resolution: Adapter must handle this as an explicit no-code completion/reconciliation path only when every operation is atomically already-applied and proof obligations can be satisfied at exact current main; otherwise block rather than fabricate a PR.

challenge.scenario: Incremental Replay invokes Sentinel integrity while CI has activated a release-unit child plan.
challenge.finding: A hardcoded root active-plan consumer would compare child execution evidence against the parent transaction and could either false-block or falsely validate the wrong authority.
challenge.resolution: Sentinel probe consumes the same SHOPERATION_ACTIVE_PLAN path after CI context validation, while the default path remains unchanged outside child mode.

challenge.scenario: A decomposed release unit contains only first-class create operations and therefore has no legitimate existing file in mustEdit.
challenge.finding: Requiring a non-empty mustEdit would force scope fabrication or make valid Unit 2 create-only units impossible to execute through child Plan Before Code.
challenge.resolution: Operational Intelligence recognizes manifest-bound releaseUnitContext and accepts a non-empty mustCreate route as the critical execution target; ordinary parent/root critical plans continue to require mustEdit.

challenge.scenario: Existing Unit 3 tests construct manifests without childDevelopmentTransaction and verification is left backward-compatible for those fixtures.
challenge.finding: A compatibility branch would preserve exactly the unbound Truth/Lifecycle acceptance path this hardening is intended to eliminate.
challenge.resolution: Make child transaction identity mandatory for VERIFIED and upgrade the canonical Unit 3 regression fixtures instead of adding a legacy exception.

challenge.scenario: Atlas reports a missing DOMAIN-QUALITY to DOMAIN-RELEASE edge because the GitHub execution adapter was created under scripts/lib/shoperation-**.
challenge.finding: The path itself assigns DOMAIN-QUALITY ownership even though the adapter owns release PR/merge/provenance execution; adding an allow edge would encode the wrong authority placement.
challenge.resolution: Move the branch-only runtime to scripts/release-unit-github-runtime.mjs, update consumers and registry references, and let the existing DOMAIN-RELEASE canonical path classify it without an execution-policy exception.

challenge.scenario: Child lifecycle support changes implementation expressions in shoperation-close-development-plan.mjs but the existing Operational Intelligence regression still asserts only the old root-only expression literals.
challenge.finding: Reference Sync correctly reports a stale machine consumer; leaving it unchanged would make proof semantics and implementation diverge.
challenge.resolution: Update the existing lifecycle regression to assert the preserved root branch plus the explicit child branch and child lifecycle artifact contract.

proofPlan: Require plan-only Plan Before Code PASS on exact branch head before implementation.
Prove child-plan projection is sealed into manifest identity and changes to child scope/gates/proof alter manifestDigest deterministically.

Run existing child-capable Knowledge/Plan/Edit-Time/Replay/Risk/Quality/TypeScript/Build/Truth/Lifecycle paths using an alternate plan path and prove ordinary root-plan transactions remain byte-compatible.

Replay parent/child identity attacks: parent Truth for child, foreign child lifecycle, mutable PR context, wrong head/base/source, stale state-ref, duplicate/open/merged PR retries, gh/git failures and merge/main drift.
Run a three-unit simulated GitHub adapter integration with injected deterministic git/gh responses, exact state-ref CAS and successor fresh-manifest replacement.
Run Edit-Time Guard and Incremental Replay, unchanged Release Risk Budget, full Quality Tests, TypeScript and Production Build.
Use external Template Factory proof only where canonical child manifest applicability requires it; producer scope remains authoritative.
Require Completion Truth VERIFIED and Lifecycle Closure for this hardening implementation itself before merge, then verify fresh main push CI/Template Factory.
After merge, run a bounded production-like release-unit rehearsal using the new adapter against non-product fixture scope before declaring the original end-to-end multi-unit objective closed.

requirements.requirement: Each release unit is bound to a deterministic manifest-sealed child Development Transaction whose existing Truth/Lifecycle evidence is exact-task and exact-head scoped while the parent transaction remains open.

forbiddenRegressions.statement: No release unit may consume parent/foreign lifecycle evidence or close the parent Development Transaction as a side effect of child verification.

requirements.requirement: The release-unit execution adapter produces exact materialization/PR/proof/merge receipts from existing git/gh and Control Plane authorities, persists progress with CAS, and cannot advance on stale or mismatched identity.

forbiddenRegressions.statement: Free-form operator PR/merge/proof receipts cannot advance canonical release-unit state without exact producer identity.

requirements.requirement: A multi-unit parent remains in EXECUTE through intermediate child closures, advances only the next unit from freshly reconciled main, and reaches closureEligible only after every unit is CLOSED before existing parent Truth/Lifecycle closure.

forbiddenRegressions.statement: Child Truth/Lifecycle completion must never imply parent Completion Truth/Lifecycle completion.

notes: Continuation/hardening of merged Unit 3 after capability-closure audit. The audit proved two remaining canonical edges: PR/merge receipts had no repository producer, and intermediate unit lifecycle evidence was not bound to a distinct child Development Transaction. This transaction closes those edges inside existing Release Transaction/Control Plane authorities. No Knowledge promotion is pre-written. Plan-only PR #958 run 37501003926 resolved canonical scope to quality-infrastructure + release-infrastructure, retained DOMAIN-QUALITY + DOMAIN-RELEASE authorities, canonical Negative Knowledge SQ-NK-002/003/005/010/012/016-023, guard digest 9a67776f, projected Release Risk 4/5 PASS, and a mandatory two-unit decomposition caused by the canonical 12-file unit limit. Consumer audit found scripts/shoperation-sentinel-integrity-probe.mjs as an additional active-plan reader reachable from Control Plane replay. Canonical scope expanded before implementation; a new Plan Before Code PASS is required. Child-plan projection audit found create-only release units cannot satisfy the current critical semantic route without fabricating mustEdit. Scope expanded to operational-intelligence validator with a child-only mustEdit-or-mustCreate rule; root critical validation remains unchanged. Verification binding necessarily changes the existing Unit 3 orchestration proof fixture. Added tests/control-plane-release-unit-orchestration.test.ts to canonical proof scope; no legacy unbound verification compatibility is permitted. Replay-proven Atlas failure ATLAS_AUTHORITY_DEPENDENCY_DRIFT on head 162fcb15 showed the GitHub adapter was placed under DOMAIN-QUALITY by scripts/lib/shoperation-** canonical ownership while its declared responsibility is release-infrastructure. Root cause is corrected by canonical path placement, not by adding an authority exception. Exact-head Plan Before Code identified the GitHub execution runtime path as scripts/lib/shoperation-release-unit-github-runtime.mjs; the stale non-lib path declaration was reconciled without changing subsystem, domain, authority, risk, or proof scope. Current Atlas-compatible implementation places the thin GitHub-bound adapter in the release-domain scripts root. Canonical plan path reconciled to scripts/release-unit-github-runtime.mjs; no capability, risk or authority scope changed. Exact-head Edit-Time/Reference Sync on 337ccb03 found tests/shoperation-operational-intelligence.test.ts as a stale lifecycle consumer after child closure support. Added it to canonical proof scope before editing.
